name: War Throne

stars.name: Sol Imperator
stars.notes: Primary star, near-solar analog providing broad habitable zone and stable luminosity. Anchor of the trinary system.

stars.name: Sol Secundus
stars.notes: Secondary star orbiting the primary at 85 AU. Its faint light provides a dim second day to the outer worlds.

stars.name: Sol Tertius
stars.notes: Distant red dwarf orbiting the pair at 340 AU. Its sole planet, tidal-locked, serves as a remote observation post.

planets.name: Foundry
planets.notes: Innermost planet orbiting Sol Imperator. Extreme heat and tidal forces drive volcanic activity. Automated smelting operations process ore in the planet's natural furnaces.

planets.name: Imperium
planets.notes: Capital world of the entire Terran military apparatus. Breathable atmosphere, temperate climate, population 1.2 billion. Seat of the Supreme Command Council and the War College of Imperium.

planets.name: Legionary
planets.notes: Earth-like world dedicated to military production and troop training. Population 420 million. Surface divided into massive training ranges, factory complexes, and garrison cities.

planets.name: Arsenal
planets.notes: Cooler terrestrial world with dense atmosphere. Population 85 million. Houses strategic weapons reserves, research laboratories, and the sector's primary military hospital system.

planets.name: Colossus
planets.notes: Enormous gas giant orbiting Sol Imperator. Its moons form a mini-system of fuel depots, repair yards, and fleet anchorages collectively housing 200,000 personnel.

planets.name: Tribune
planets.notes: Second gas giant orbiting between Sol Imperator and Sol Secundus. Ring system contains automated defense platforms.

planets.name: Outwatch
planets.notes: Frozen world in the gravitational influence of Sol Secundus. Deep-space early warning systems and emergency fleet dispersal coordinates.

planets.name: Farthest Post
planets.notes: Tidal-locked world orbiting Sol Tertius. The permanently dark hemisphere houses a classified signals intelligence facility monitoring communications across the Imperial Core.

anomalies.name: The Trinary Dance
anomalies.notes: The three-star configuration creates complex gravitational harmonics that generate multiple stable and unstable Lagrange points. The stable points are used as fleet staging areas; the unstable ones serve as natural barriers to uncontrolled approach.

anomalies.name: The Emperor's Shadow
anomalies.location: Between Sol Imperator and Sol Secundus
anomalies.notes: A region where the combined stellar winds create electromagnetic interference so dense that no sensor system can penetrate it. Used to conceal fleet movements and classified installations.

asteroid_belts.name: The Iron Ring
asteroid_belts.notes: Extraordinarily metal-rich asteroid belt that supplies the raw materials for the system's massive shipbuilding industry. Over 10,000 mining operations active at any given time.

asteroid_belts.name: The Outer Palisade
asteroid_belts.location: Between Sol Secundus and Sol Tertius influence zones
asteroid_belts.notes: Dispersed belt of ice and rock marking the boundary between the secondary and tertiary star's domains. Seeded with automated defense platforms.

stations.name: Supreme Command Orbital
stations.notes: The single most important military installation in human space. Houses the Supreme Command Council, strategic war planning, and the master communications array linking all Terran military assets.

stations.name: Forge Colossus
stations.location: Orbital complex spanning multiple moons of Colossus
stations.notes: The largest shipyard in existence, spanning three moons with twenty capital-ship construction slips. Produces the backbone of the Terran fleet.

stations.name: War Academy Station
stations.notes: Premier officer training facility. Graduates serve in command positions across the fleet. Includes zero-gravity combat simulation and tactical war gaming complexes.

stations.name: Hospital Ship Mercy Eternal
stations.notes: Massive medical station serving as the primary rehabilitation and trauma center for casualties from across the sector.

stations.name: Bastion Anchorage
stations.location: Stable Lagrange point between Sol Imperator and Sol Secundus
stations.notes: Permanent fleet anchorage where reserve battle groups maintain readiness. Can surge sixty capital ships within four hours of activation order.

faction_control.notes: The capital military system of the Terran domain. Security is absolute. Unauthorized entry is treated as an act of war. Even allied diplomatic vessels require advance clearance through multiple security layers.

history: Founded in 2298 as the first purpose-built military capital system, War Throne was selected for its trinary configuration, which provides natural defensive advantages, abundant resources, and multiple habitable worlds capable of supporting a massive permanent military population.

The system served as the command center for the Unification Campaigns of 2340-2380 that brought the outer colonies under Terran authority, and every major military operation since has been planned and directed from Supreme Command Orbital above Imperium.

In 2655, the War Throne Conspiracy—an attempted coup by a cabal of senior admirals seeking to replace civilian oversight with permanent military rule—was narrowly thwarted. The conspirators were tried and executed, but the incident raised questions about the concentration of military power in a single system that have never been fully resolved.
description: War Throne is the capital system of Terran military power, and it looks the part. Three stars—yellow, orange, and red—orbit each other in a gravitational dance that has been exploited to create one of the most formidable defensive positions in known space. Eight worlds serve the war machine with a combined military and support population exceeding 1.7 billion. Imperium alone is home to 1.2 billion people, its surface a vast expanse of command centers, government buildings, and military academies linked by maglev networks that run with the precision of a well-drilled regiment. The system is not merely defended; it is defense incarnate.

The military infrastructure of War Throne is without parallel. Supreme Command Orbital directs operations across the entirety of Terran-controlled space. Forge Colossus builds the warships. War Academy Station trains the officers. Bastion Anchorage holds a reserve fleet that could conquer a sector by itself. The Iron Ring asteroid belt feeds raw materials to shipyards that never stop producing. The system's output in ships, soldiers, and strategic planning is the foundation upon which Terran dominance rests. Remove War Throne, and the structure collapses.

But empires built on military might carry a particular vulnerability: the people who wield the weapons may decide they should also wield the power. The War Throne Conspiracy of 2655 was officially a contained incident involving a handful of rogue admirals, but persistent rumors suggest the rot went deeper than the official narrative admits. Meanwhile, the Emperor's Shadow—the sensor-opaque region between the primary and secondary stars—has become a source of unease. Fleet Intelligence cannot fully monitor what moves through it, and there are those who believe that if another conspiracy is brewing, it is hiding there, in the one place in the system where Supreme Command cannot see.
